To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new, efficient, and versatile numerical tool that can be used to study the aerodynamics of flapping wings and that we have used this tool to predict lift and power for a hovering Drosphila, a flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle (MAV), and a flapping-wing MAV with aeroelastic deformations.

we have successfully developed a new numerical-simulation tool to model the unsteady nonlinear aeroelastic dynamics of flying insects and biologically inspired flappers, and that the results are in close agreement to the results obtained with the Euler equations, the results obtained with a vortex-lattice model, and with experimental data.
we have extended a well-known numerical tool to study unsteady, nonlinear aerodynamics of flapping wings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the aerodynamic analysis of hovering insects and small birds and biologically inspired flapped-wing micro air vehicles (MAVs).
the development of a numerical tool that will allow us to predict the aerodynamics of flapping wings and, in turn, provide the basis for the design of flapping-wing micro-air vehicles.
the numerical simulation of unsteady flows around flapping wings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the numerical method is a useful tool to predict the aerodynamic forces acting on a flapping wing.
the present method provides a good compromise between computational cost (which is low) and fidelity (which is high).
the present numerical model is capable of predicting the unsteady aerodynamic characteristics of flapping wings and is ideally suited for use in aeroelastic analyses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a numerical-simulation tool that is well suited to model the unsteady aerodynamics of flying small insects and small birds.
the numerical model is a powerful and versatile tool to study the aerodynamics and flight of flapping-wing insects and micro air vehicles.
we developed a new numerical model that can be used for the aerodynamic analysis of a wide variety of flapping wing configurations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple, low-order numerical model can be used to study the flowfield around flapping wings and predict lift.
a simple unsteady vortex-latitude model with a twist and a chordwise variation in the circulation distribution is able to capture the essential features of the flowfield around a flapping wing.
the unsteady flow around a flapping wing can be modeled with reasonable accuracy using the vortex-lattice method, provided the wing kinematics are accurately modeled.
